why: The two statements differ in a hypothesis. A states the metrizability of |A| and |E_A|, the local isomorphism property of the top target map, the top inversion isomorphism and the top multiplication only under the added hypothesis IsCompatible; the top target map tgtSq is a strong bundle map only under it (isStrongBundleMap_tgtSq). B assumes no compatibility, and the project shows IsCompatible is a hypothesis beyond Definitions 19.8.4/19.8.5. Under IsCompatible all of B follows from A (A_to_B_of_compatible, proved and rt_check OK). It uses the conjunct SquareBasicConstruction.theorem_19_8_22_hyp, with Kb = bundleG via isStrongBundleIso_altH, and the topologies generated by NatOpenA, NatOpenEA and NatOpenEB are equal to the project's natTopA, natTopEA and natTopEB. Whether B holds without compatibility is not settled here. B_to_A is not obtained: A also contains the commutation of the structure maps with m̂, p̂ and p, the formulas for mulSq and mulG, the properness of the squares over the fibred products, and three general lemmas on proper strong bundle covering squares. B does not state these, and its Kb is existential.
B_issue: As its author notes, B's top-level multiplication clause is quantified over proofs of IsCompatible, so it is vacuous when compatibility does not hold. B also omits the commutation of the structure maps with p and p̂ ('between proper squares').
overlap: No direction proved, so there is no rt_overlap. rt_check OK for A_to_B_of_compatible: no item theorem is reached; isStrongBundleIso_altH belongs to V19_97, not this item.

main.note: The main conjunct alone gives B under IsCompatible (A_to_B_of_compatible uses only it). B lacks IsCompatible, and B does not give the main conjunct's equalities m̂∘ι̂ = ι∘m̂ etc. or the statements about the project's bundleG.
